articles.title: Verify SMN backups
articles.searchText: verify smn backups a useful backup is one you can find and verify here s how to check your archives without accidentally restoring data before you begin access to backup features requires the appropriate account permissions follow the steps open settings maintenance open the backup tab when it is available to your account review the archive inventory statuses and verification results if authorized start a backup from the business interface and verify its outcome manually mark backup done once your procedure has been checked restore safeguards an available or verified backup does not mean restoration is authorized follow smn s displayed security checks do not replace the user interface with manual commands help checklist progress is local to the browser and is not included in backup archives

articles.title: Prepare the team calendar
articles.searchText: prepare the team calendar a reliable calendar helps plan cycles and understand availability start by checking the team s information before making decisions before you begin a team must exist editing requires the appropriate privileges follow the steps open the team calendar and select your team context review displayed days cycle periods absences and available calendar data if your role allows it review individual calendars and assignments under team members if the installation includes a scrum team an administrator can review working day settings from settings this screen is not intended for kanban only installations check results after making changes in the business screens then manually mark calendar done note absences public holidays and availability can differ between team members viewing a calendar does not automatically verify capacity

articles.title: Dashboard: keep your team on course
articles.searchText: dashboard keep your team on course your dashboard is the place to start your day in a quick glance you can find the current cycle see progress and spot anything worth discussing with the team start with the right context 1 open the dashboard from the main navigation 2 check the team and product in the header switch context if you work with multiple teams 3 check the selected cycle and dates in scrum this is a sprint in kanban a period 4 explore goals indicators and tracking blocks start with the information that might require a decision a useful habit before discussing a number in a daily or review always confirm which team and cycle it belongs to make sense of your indicators a number on its own never tells the whole story look for changes and compare them with what the team is experiencing available capacity tickets impediments or recent decisions something looks surprising open its details or review the indicator definition a value is missing check the cycle and source data an empty value is not zero a block is not useful consider whether its configuration should change make the dashboard your own when your permissions allow it open dashboard builder using the available customization action blocks are arranged in rows select information adjust titles and presentation then save return to the dashboard and check that the blocks tell a clear story where are we what is slowing us down and what should we do next if something does not appear 1 check the selected team and cycle 2 confirm the required source data exists tickets assignments or indicators 3 read the indicator definition before assuming something is broken you are done when you can find the cycle interpret the main blocks and explain where the displayed figures come from

articles.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
articles.searchText: faq and troubleshooting missing screen rejected import or empty indicator start here for practical checks that help you understand what s happening a screen or action is missing some operations require administrator permissions a specific team or a scrum kanban mode review your account and active team do not bypass access checks with direct urls see the first time setup guide or ask an administrator why does ticket csv import fail under tickets the csv must include id type resume priority status sp former jira column names are not supported check the date csv syntax and ticket identifiers as well refer to the tickets article in help why do i need to confirm replacement another snapshot already exists for the selected date smn asks for explicit confirmation before replacement recheck the file and date concurrent changes may require confirmation again why is ticket comparison unavailable at least two compatible snapshots are needed in the selected context why are sprints unavailable check that the installation team uses scrum and that you have permission to access it kanban teams use their own periods why is an indicator value missing review team and cycle context manually entered values formulas and source data a missing value is not automatically zero indicator settings can be restricted to administrators why can t a backup be restored if your account has the necessary permissions you can review archive inventory and restoration checks under settings maintenance an existing archive does not automatically authorize restoration mandatory safeguards must pass why did my help checkmarks disappear on another computer checklist progress is stored locally in the browser it is not synchronized or included in smn backups a new browser profile or origin starts without previous checkmarks what if help search fails try searching again from the help center when an index is unavailable accessible articles can still be opened from their categories the bundled documentation does not require an external service

articles.title: General settings: language, appearance and calendar reference
articles.searchText: general settings language appearance and calendar reference make smn feel right for your everyday work language appearance and calendar settings help keep the interface comfortable and consistent access and prerequisites open general settings using an authorized administrator account settings are saved by this business form not by the help center understand the three tabs general view the read only agile mode and product select a reference country from the list when needed language choose french or english from the currently available languages appearance choose the light or dark theme and an offered palette ocean forest violet or red purple agile mode and product are fixed information in this form they cannot be edited here change and save settings 1 open the tab for the setting you want to change 2 choose the desired value from its selector for the reference country you can leave the selection empty when offered 3 an alert indicates unsaved changes select save the button is disabled when nothing changed or while saving 4 read the confirmation or error message display settings such as language theme or palette may refresh the interface after saving 5 if needed use reload to restore the currently saved values check the revision or update date displayed by the form errors and precautions revision conflict settings changed since the form loaded reload and review the latest values before trying again invalid value choose an allowed option and retry load or network error use the retry action and check the local connection to smn pending edits save or discard your changes before leaving smn warns about unsaved drafts access denied a user without administrative rights must not attempt to change settings check the result confirm the intended values are saved and displayed the help center checklist does not validate settings automatically mark general done only after your own review

articles.title: Dynamic indicators
articles.searchText: dynamic indicators indicators help you understand trends not just numbers this guide shows how to read them in context and check their sources before you begin you must be signed in and have access to at least one team editing the catalog and permissions depends on your account role view indicators open indicators select an authorized team and review its scrum or kanban indicators check cycle values and the available displays in the relevant screens indicators may use manual values or formulas a missing value is not necessarily zero administration an administrator can review indicator settings from settings including definitions and permissions before changing a formula inspect its dependencies and potential effects on dashboards and reports if an action is unavailable review your role and selected team rather than bypassing access checks common issues no indicator or value review team cycle context permissions and the underlying data needed for calculation unexpected result check the formula and dependencies before treating it as a defect access denied ask an administrator to review your permissions the help center never edits indicators or formulas

articles.title: Jira link
articles.searchText: jira link this menu lets you define your jira instance address smn uses it to reconstruct ticket urls after tickets have been imported from a csv file

articles.title: Prepare Kanban periods
articles.searchText: prepare kanban periods kanban periods give your tracking a useful time frame here s how to prepare them without confusing them with scrum sprints before you begin you need access to a kanban team managing periods requires the appropriate permissions follow the steps open kanban periods review existing periods and the selected team context if authorized use the period creation form verify displayed details and dates after saving manually mark cadence done once the periods are ready scrum and kanban a kanban period is not a scrum sprint help does not create any period

articles.title: Links: find and manage team resources
articles.searchText: links find and manage team resources keep your team s useful resources close at hand boards documents tools and shared spaces links help you find them without hunting through bookmarks access links open links from the navigation when your administrator account is authorized the screen groups team specific links and accessible cross team links find and open a link 1 confirm the team name in the header 2 select cards or list view 3 search by link title then narrow results using scope and category filters 4 sort by title category or most recent date as needed 5 select open on a result to open the destination in a new tab add or edit a link with management permission 1 select add in the header 2 fill in the form including the title destination address and available scope or category options 3 save and find the new entry in the list 4 use the edit action on an existing card or row to change it verify its title and destination after saving for deletion use the dedicated action and read the confirmation if a conflict or access error occurs refresh and review the situation instead of forcing it categories under settings link categories and related settings are maintained separately in settings links use that screen to prepare categories before assigning them to links in the main module why manage links in smn smn keeps relevant resources easy to find cross team or team scope establishes their context while categories support filtering smn does not automatically analyze an external website just because its address has been saved check the result you can find the right link open its destination and when authorized change its classification reading this guide does not modify a link

articles.title: Members: build a reliable picture of team capacity
articles.searchText: members build a reliable picture of team capacity a team member is more than a name on a roster their profile assignment work schedule country and absences help smn represent team availability taking time to check this information prevents misleading sprint capacity figures good habit start with members already in smn update existing records instead of creating duplicates 1 find the right team members 1 open team members and check the selected team 2 choose cards for browsing profiles or list to compare people 3 use name role function and status filters then select filter 4 review active and inactive groups someone who has left the team may still belong in its history 5 open a member record to review the details cards list is a local display preference it does not modify assignments 2 complete the profile why each field matters identity and professional function display name identifies the person in the roster and records email address optional contact information where relevant it does not determine team assignment professional function describes the person s job or specialty it is different from their agile role someone may divide their activity between development scrum master and product owner responsibilities location determines the national holiday calendar open location on the member record and review country two letter iso code identifies the member s country and the matching national public holidays region adds geographical context city identifies the usual working location time zone iana provides the member s time zone reference effective date indicates when the location version takes effect do you need to enter public holidays manually not for national holidays already included in smn s reference data the member calendar automatically looks up holidays for the country stored on that member s location record rather than using the installation country or another person s location example a team may include one person in france and another in india each calendar should show the national holidays of the corresponding country when those dates are included in smn s reference data always check the country not just the city or time zone important local or regional holidays are not guaranteed to be available check the calendar when a particular non working day matters for planning 3 define team assignment and agile roles open assignment assignment start and end dates determine when a person belongs to the team including for historical sprints understand the percentages contract percentage reference working time proportion allocation percentage the part assigned to the team the form checks that allocation does not exceed contract percentage contribution percentage describes the contribution configured for planning role distribution allocates 100 across scrum master product owner and developer as required by the form effective date records when a change becomes applicable preserving dated assignment versions example a part time employee may be assigned to the team for only part of their working time and split their responsibilities between development and scrum master duties their name alone cannot determine development capacity joining leaving and history 1 review the assignment start date 2 when a person leaves enter the end date and an optional reason 3 record changes of responsibility with a new dated version 4 correct a historical revision only to fix an earlier mistake ending an assignment is not the same as deleting the member 4 configure working days and half days open calendar then edit work calendar the form shows monday through sunday with two slots per day morning worked check when the member normally works in the morning afternoon worked check when the member normally works in the afternoon effective date defines when this weekly pattern starts to apply half day slots help represent a non working wednesday afternoon or a part time schedule when no schedule has been saved smn can suggest a monday to friday week with both half days worked a suggestion is not a validated schedule adjust and save it based on the person s real working pattern planning tip avoid copying one member s working week to everyone two developers with identical contract percentages may follow different schedules 5 check absences and calendar exceptions from the member record review the calendar and absences the absence form includes start and end dates half day slots a category a reason and whether the absence is planned or unplanned calendar exceptions capture one off changes to the normal working week national holidays available in smn are looked up automatically from the member s country so you do not need to create a manual absence for each supported holiday avoid duplicate absences and ensure dates fall within the relevant team assignment be careful with historical changes affecting closed sprints 6 how member information feeds team capacity team capacity is not simply headcount multiplied by sprint days several pieces of information matter together 1 assignment period is the member part of this team on the relevant dates 2 contract allocation and contribution how much activity should be considered 3 agile roles how is work distributed across development scrum master and product owner duties 4 personal work calendar which days and half days are worked 5 country and public holidays which national holidays apply to this member 6 absences and exceptions what changes the available working time these inputs inform availability worked day and capacity information in smn the exact calculation depends on the indicator s definition total person day capacity and development capacity need not include the same activities example a sprint covers ten usual working days one member only joins in week two another does not work wednesday afternoons and a third has a national holiday counting three people for ten full days would overstate availability 7 when capacity or holidays look wrong capacity too high check assignment end dates working patterns and missing absences capacity too low check assignment dates unchecked half days percentages and recorded absences missing public holiday verify the member s country code and that the holiday exists in smn s reference data wrong country s holiday correct the member s location not the global installation country unexpected historical result review dated versions and closed sprint states some closed sprint indicators may need to be refreshed by closing the sprint again after a correction your final check ask yourself are assignment dates correct do contract and role percentages reflect reality is the work schedule accurate does the country match the holiday calendar have absences been reviewed once these details are reliable your team is in a better position to plan sprints and interpret capacity indicators

articles.title: Getting started with SMN: set up your first team step by step
articles.searchText: getting started with smn set up your first team step by step this walkthrough guides you from initial settings to your first useful tracking view take it at your own pace the goal is a working smn not merely checked boxes you have just signed in to smn before using sprints or kanban periods for meaningful tracking you need to prepare some information this walkthrough explains what to configure why it matters how smn uses it and how to check the outcome start by checking teams and members already present an existing or restored installation may contain data to customize a fresh native v33 installation on an empty database does not automatically create teams or members this guide supports both situations you can revisit any step administrator only actions must be performed by an authorized account as a standard user follow the steps available to you and ask your administrator to prepare the others the help center also includes a first setup checklist use read guide to go deeper into each topic and open screen to perform the task you manually mark a step done smn never interprets reading the article as proof of completion step 1 review general settings why starting with the appropriate language appearance and reference country helps keep subsequent settings consistent what to do administrator under settings general review the displayed agile mode and product these fields are read only in this form under general choose a reference country if required under language select french or english under appearance choose the light or dark theme and a palette select save if anything changed and check the confirmation and saved values how smn uses it the application stores general settings applies display preferences and uses reference settings in the views that support them you cannot change the agile mode in this form check before continuing your language theme and selected country appear correctly after saving step 2 review and customize your team why smn links cycles members and business data to a team check what is already there first then tailor it to your real situation creating another team when one already exists would duplicate it what to do administrator open settings teams and inspect the list use filters if necessary to find active or archived teams if a team already exists select it to open the edit dialog update its name product vision and goal to reflect your real team check its scrum or kanban mode which determines available cycles smn may prevent a mode change for an existing team respect that restriction only if no usable team exists choose create team from the header then enter the same information and select the appropriate agile mode save and confirm the team appears correctly in the list select it elsewhere when smn asks for team context how smn uses it smn uses the team to associate members cycles and business information agile mode controls scrum or kanban functionality while product details appear in the views and reports that support them check you have the right team customized without duplicates with the expected agile mode and product details step 3 review existing members and complete assignments why members roles and assignment dates determine who belongs to the team at a given time review and customize existing profiles instead of recreating them what to do administrator open team members for the selected team check existing members first including active and inactive groups in cards or list view if your installation contains example people or profiles open their records and adapt them to your real team do not assume that every installation contains the same number of members check each member s name function city and country roles and assignments check assignment start and end dates an inactive member or former assignment is not the same as a deleted profile choose add member only if someone is missing then complete the new profile and assignments return to the list and review active inactive groups and filters how smn uses it profiles and assignment periods support team information calendars and capacity interpretation where those features are available check existing profiles have been reviewed or customized missing members added without duplicates and assignment periods checked step 4 review working days calendar and absences why working days assignments and absences affect how team availability is interpreted a wrong date or country can make capacity information misleading what to do if your installation contains a scrum team and you are an administrator review working days settings and the available work slot options open the team calendar for the relevant team review displayed days recorded absences and cycle information where available compare member assignment dates and location details with the calendar if no cycle exists yet review the settings you can and return after the next step some views need a selected period how smn uses it calendar and absence information appear in the relevant views and help interpret availability and capacity alongside team assignments and work rules check known working days and absences are consistent merely viewing the calendar does not validate capacity automatically step 5 prepare your first scrum or kanban cycle why a cycle provides the time frame for tracking work and analyzing indicators its setup depends on the team s agile mode what to do follow only the branch matching your team s agile mode for a scrum team open sprints and choose the relevant team review existing sprints if you are an administrator use generate when offered check cadence dates and statuses before confirming open the sprint from the list to review its period for a kanban team open kanban periods in the correct team context review existing periods as an administrator choose a start date in the creation form check the calculated start end and time zone and the suggested period name before confirming review the creation message if a period overlaps another correct the dates instead of forcing creation how smn uses it tracking information is associated with scrum sprints or kanban periods the available screens and some checklist steps adapt to the selected agile mode check an appropriate cycle is available and its dates are correct return to the calendar afterward to check period dependent information step 6 prepare your first ticket data why having a team and cycle is only the foundation tickets provide a snapshot of actual work and may be compared over time what to do open tickets for the chosen team and cycle if you have a csv file and the necessary rights prepare these required columns id type resume priority status sp select import csv choose the file and its reference date then run validation correct any errors if a snapshot already exists on that date carefully review the replacement prompt open the imported snapshot comparison becomes useful after multiple compatible snapshots have been saved how smn uses it it stores ticket snapshots for browsing and when sufficient data exists comparison ticket information can feed the views and indicators that use it check the expected snapshot appears on the correct date with the expected tickets if you have no csv yet leave the step to do rather than inventing data step 7 explore indicators and initial reports why dashboards and reports become useful when teams cycles and initial data are available check their sources before drawing conclusions what to do review indicators available to your team confirm the selected cycle and distinguish a missing value from zero open reports and browse reports templates tags and archives if the administrator action new report is available select the cycle template title and language for an office document select a word or powerpoint template review its data sources and tags and choose generate to download or save to keep the document open the result and check what was populated missing data must not be assumed to be zero how smn uses it smn uses available data according to configured indicators and document templates then generates or stores documents based on the chosen action check you can find an indicator or report and identify any data still required for useful reporting step 8 protect your setup with a backup why once the first data has been entered a verified backup helps protect your work including when moving to another computer what to do authorized administrator open settings maintenance then backups when available review the archive list and verification results if backup creation is authorized in the interface perform one and check its result do not confuse backup available with restoration authorized restoration remains subject to the installation s safety checks how smn uses it maintenance features manage archives and related verification according to the installation s safety rules the checklist marks stored in your browser are not included in backups check you know how to verify an archive and have reviewed its status without performing an unnecessary restoration your first setup is ready when your team exists members and assignments make sense a calendar and a cycle have been checked and you know where to enter ticket information inspect indicators and prepare reports backups protect this foundation return to the checklist in the help center mark each applicable step in progress or done self declared after checking it yourself steps outside your role are filtered and no checkbox performs business configuration progress remains in this browser on this installation

articles.title: Registers: risks, impediments, dependencies, decisions, actions and highlights
articles.searchText: registers risks impediments dependencies decisions actions and highlights an early risk or a well recorded decision can prevent confusion later use registries to make important team information visible and actionable access registers open registers after selecting a team your account can access the data shown depends on the team and when offered the selected cycle the main list distinguishes risks impediments and dependencies smn also supports decisions actions and highlights including in related record details and journals do not expect six separate tabs on the main list browse and find an entry on the list choose an available category or use the search and filters provided status cycle sorting and other criteria visible according to your permissions open a record to review its title date status description and where available type specific details relationships and journal check the team and cycle before comparing information the list can be empty even when records exist in another context users without management permission can view entries in read only mode editing and deletion actions are not shown to them understand the six types risk a risk describes something that might happen its statuses are open and resolved you can also provide a probability an impact and a roam response during creation these assessments are separate from the risk s status impediment an impediment describes a difficulty that has occurred its possible statuses are open in progress resolved and abandoned review the status changes and the details recorded in its entry dependency a dependency describes coordination between a requester and a contributor each associated with the local team or an external party it can also be marked at risk its statuses are open in progress satisfied and cancelled if you enter the parties in the form the requester and contributor must be specified consistently an external party requires a name decision a decision records a choice and where provided its rationale it can reference a previous decision that it replaces the statuses are active replaced and cancelled decisions can also be found through related record journals or relationships follow the creation context instead of expecting them among the main category tabs action an action represents work or follow up to perform its statuses are to do in progress completed and cancelled depending on your permissions its record may display links to other items and a tracking history highlight a highlight records a notable event or piece of information it uses the recorded status it may be created or found through a related journal depending on the actions provided by that record it does not create a new main list tab create edit or delete if your account offers the create action open the creation dialog and select a type available in that context the form asks for a title date and status then shows additional fields for the chosen type available types may be restricted when creation starts from a journal use the displayed options rather than trying to force an unavailable type with appropriate permissions open a record and use the available edit actions permanent deletion is separate from reading a record it requires management permission and can be refused when linked data a conflict or a protection prevents the operation review the record and consequences before confirming reading this article does not create update or delete any entry common issues no entries check the team cycle category and filters before assuming information is missing action not shown your role or the creation context may restrict available actions and types form rejected verify the title required fields and for dependencies the requester and contributor deletion rejected review the record s message and linked items do not bypass a protective refusal

articles.title: Reports: view, create and generate documents
articles.searchText: reports view create and generate documents a good report tells the story of what happened and helps decide what comes next learn to turn smn data into useful documents without losing sight of the sources access and scope open reports after signing in and select an authorized team when the screen provides that option results depend on the team sprint or cycle and your account permissions creating a new report from the header is restricted to administrators when the screen allows it understand the four tabs reports browse saved documents use search sprint or cycle filters and any available status filter then open a report with the read action templates browse available office templates the catalog detects word and powerpoint templates in smn s configured folders tags read the available office expressions the tag configurator helps you build and copy a tag for a simple value indicator row or chart archives browse archived items within your authorized context available filters include searching and cycle selection the four tabs are separate workflows not mandatory steps read an existing report 1 on reports choose the relevant cycle or leave all to browse the current scope 2 enter a search phrase if needed apply filters and review the results 3 check the title sprint or cycle model status and update date 4 open the document using its read action if nothing appears check the team and filters first create a report in smn if you are an administrator and new report is available 1 open the creation dialog from the report center header 2 choose an available sprint or cycle and template 3 enter the title and choose french or english 4 select create the action may be disabled when no suitable cycle or template exists or a required field is missing 5 find the new report in the list and review its content creating it does not guarantee that all model data is available generate an office document from a template on templates after selecting a word or powerpoint model 1 select the cycle offered by the form and enter a filename 2 choose the document language and when available a chart style 3 if the template uses ticket data select the ticket snapshots required by the form 4 choose generate to download a file or save to place it in smn s reports folder these are separate actions 5 if saving detects an existing file review the overwrite confirmation before proceeding inspect the generated document afterward generation may fail when a model or data source is unavailable a tag is invalid or the ticket selection is unsuitable fix the fields or template before trying again do not treat missing data as zero build template tags on tags open the configurator and choose a family and its available options copy the generated expression into your office template table tags may support sorting chart tags offer compatible chart types and styles for the selected indicators check team data availability before using indicator tags result and limitations generating and saving reports are business operations separate from reading help help center progress is self declared mark reports done only after checking your own output opening this guide never generates a document

articles.title: Plan and generate your Scrum sprints
articles.searchText: plan and generate your scrum sprints preparing your next sprint or a whole series smn helps you build a consistent sprint calendar without entering every date by hand the key is to choose the right starting point review the proposal and confirm only when everything looks correct camille s tip check existing sprints before creating any your installation may already contain sample sprints you can explore 1 find your team s sprints 1 open sprints from the navigation 2 check the team shown in the header this is the context for the sprint list 3 explore the all active planned finished and closed status filters 4 use search and sort when the list gets longer select a sprint name to open its details why start here creating another series without checking the current schedule can lead to overlaps or unnecessary sprints if the sprint already exists open it instead of generating a duplicate before generating check your team s sprint cadence where do the dates come from the wizard uses settings team cadence sprint you do not need to re enter each sprint s duration weekdays or times smn reads the selected scrum team s duration in weeks start day and time end day and time and time zone what if you have never configured the cadence smn can automatically create the missing cadence configuration using these default values duration 2 weeks start monday at 09 00 end friday at 18 00 in the second week time zone europe paris before generating a series open the team s cadence settings and check these values defaults make it possible to get started but may not reflect your team s actual working rhythm practical example with the default cadence a wednesday start date is aligned to the following monday the first sprint then ends on the friday of the second week at 18 00 when generating three sprints smn calculates subsequent periods from the same cadence if you have already customized the cadence your saved values take precedence over these defaults always inspect the preview before creating anything if a technical problem prevents the settings from being read or prepared the preview reports an error and generation should not be confirmed 2 open the generation wizard with administrator permissions select generate from the list header the wizard has three stages configure preview and confirm what each field means number of sprints choose how many sprints to create together from 1 to 6 start with 1 while exploring select more when planning several iterations ahead start date enter the start date of the first sprint smn may suggest a date but you should check it before continuing the other dates are calculated using the configured cadence cadence the configured duration weekdays times and time zone determine the proposed periods these settings are not all entered in this wizard if the calculated dates seem wrong review the cadence settings before confirming example to plan three consecutive sprints enter 3 for the number of sprints and choose the first start date smn proposes three periods for review their actual dates depend on your team s cadence select show preview to continue you are still reviewing a proposal no sprint has been confirmed yet 3 review the preview carefully the preview is your opportunity to catch mistakes before they become part of your schedule sprint name smn proposes a name that you can edit up to 160 characters use a consistent naming convention so teammates can find each sprint easily start and end dates check the calculated periods and the displayed time zone pay particular attention to the first and last dates and the transition between periods conflicts this column identifies overlaps with existing or proposed sprints if a conflict appears return to configuration and adjust the proposal ceremony templates active templates may be listed so you know which ceremony templates are available for generation historical ceremonies when working with past dates an additional choice may appear read the warning carefully it concerns historical ceremony handling not sprint duration changed a name or an option select refresh preview the wizard requires an up to date proposal before you can proceed 4 confirm the generation 1 check the number names dates and any blocking conflicts 2 select continue to reach the confirmation stage 3 review the sprint names and any warning displayed 4 select create only when you are satisfied smn returns to the sprint list find the new sprints and open one to inspect its saved details 5 troubleshooting generate is missing creating sprints requires administrator permissions the dates look wrong review the starting date and configured cadence before confirming a conflict is shown check sprints already scheduled for those dates and update your proposal you edited a sprint name select refresh preview before continuing the sprints page is unavailable check that the installation uses scrum mode and you have the necessary access kanban periods follow a different process your final check you should be able to answer which sprints exist what dates do they cover and are they in the right team context once you can answer those questions your sprint calendar is ready remember this guide does not create sprints creation happens only in smn s wizard after you confirm the operation

articles.title: Your team: start with what is already there
articles.searchText: your team start with what is already there before tracking your first sprint take a few minutes to make sure smn reflects your real team there is no need to recreate everything check existing teams first depending on the installation or restore process teams may already be present a fresh native v33 installation with an empty database does not create a team automatically changes here require administrator permissions already have a team make it yours 1 open settings teams 2 find the team you want use search or the active archived filter if needed 3 select the team to open its edit form 4 adapt its name product vision and goal to your work 5 review the scrum or kanban mode it determines which cycles are available and may be locked for an existing team 6 save and confirm the updated details in the list an existing team is usually a better starting point than a duplicate if agile mode cannot be changed review the situation before creating another team no suitable team yet create one 1 in settings teams choose create team in the header 2 enter a recognizable name and select scrum or kanban 3 add the product vision and goal using the information available today 4 confirm then find the new team in the list why these details matter agile mode determines whether smn uses sprints or kanban periods the team also provides the context for members cycles tracking data and reports you can refine details later for now the most important thing is having the right team selected your final check the team name and agile mode are correct product information has been reviewed and there are no duplicates you are ready to move on to team members

articles.title: Tickets / CSV: turn your exports into metrics and history
articles.searchText: tickets csv turn your exports into metrics and history a csv file is more than a list of issues imported into smn at the right moment it becomes a dated snapshot of a sprint or kanban period smn calculates statistics from it supports comparisons over time and can reuse selected snapshots in reports camille s tip think of each import as a measurement over time a snapshot at the start of a sprint and another at the end are much more informative than a single file 1 understand what this module gives you your workflow prepare the csv import a snapshot inspect automatically calculated metrics then compare and reuse the data automatically calculated ticket metrics in browse consultation smn can calculate ticket count number of tickets in the snapshot completed tickets tickets recognized as completed based on their status story point sum sum of usable numeric estimates estimated and unestimated tickets insight into estimation completeness breakdowns ticket counts and story points by type status and id prefix metrics can refer to all tickets or the currently filtered tickets always check the selected scope before quoting a figure using the results in smn indicators the indicators action opens the configured indicators for the selected cycle where authorized users can enter manual indicator values important distinction ticket statistics are calculated automatically in browse but they are not automatically copied into every manual indicator you can use the result as a reference when entering an appropriate manual kpi formula based indicators follow their own definitions example filter by bug and obtain 12 tickets if your indicator catalog includes a manual sprint bug count kpi you can use 12 as a reference while noting the snapshot date and filter scope 2 prepare the expected csv the first line must contain these six required column names older jira header labels are not used id type resume priority status sp what the columns mean id unique issue id such as proj 123 it identifies tickets across snapshots and helps reconstruct jira links when configured type ticket type such as story bug or task resume summary or title priority
